However, the death of her son Dylan led her down a dark path, which resulted in her family falling apart and her looking to Dr. Gabriela Torabi for assistance. In the wake of Cal's death, she spearheaded the investigation into finding his murderer, while also burying his monstrous misdeeds. With the stocks moving in her favor, within a year she is worth 34 billion, making her the richest self-made woman in the world. Not long after, about a year later, also 12 years before the catastrophic event, Sinatra gathers some of the world's greatest intellectuals to enlist in their help to build an underground city.[1] Sinatra in the hospital Sinatra and Tim would go on to have two children, their son Dylan and daughter Hadley. The former of the two unfortunately falls ill one day at the grocery store and dies from an unspecified illness after receiving more than a year and a half of treatment. With his time on earth coming to an end, Sinatra is introduced to world-class therapist and grief specialist Dr. Gabriela Torabi to deal with his death. During Dylan's final days in the hospital, while in bed, he asks if he's going to heaven. Her eyes fill with tears as she admits that he is. When asked what does she think it'll be like, she tells him that it's anything he wants it to be. Dylan wants heaven to be just like earth, but with more horse ride. Soon after, Dylan dies and Sinatra receives counseling. Six months later, Sinatra seeks out Gabriela for more help. She and her marriage were broken forever, but she still had a business to attend to, as well as her daughter. Sinatra had no desire to be healed. She simply needed to be functional and offered to pay Gabriela generously for her services. Six more months later, just a year after Dylan's death, she runs into Cal at the international finance summit while learning about a nearing environmental catastrophe.[1] The end of the world[] Sinatra boards the plane with Cal and the other billionaires on the day of the extinction-level disaster. Cal tells her about the nuclear football. The device that allows him to unilaterally launch America's entire nuclear arsenal. Everybody knows about the football and the red code but the blue code is the ultimate fail-safe. A linked array of global EMPs in satellites, submarines, missiles etc that would fry every electronic circuit on Earth. Microwaves, computers. Even its own satellites. But it would also disable the nukes, maybe even in midair. It's a switch that would shut off the world. Unfortunately, it would also take the planet back 500 years. But that was better than the alternative because it would give people a chance. Sinatra advises President Bradford against using the blue code, arguing that he will also be harming the bunker, as it relies on outside sensors for communication, for the safety of the city, so that they know when it's safe out there, leaving them blind and vulnerable, but he does it regardless.[2] Dealing with Cal's death[] With the President Bradford having been murdered in his own home, Sinatra is left to corral the board of concerned billionaires and prepare them for ahead. Afterward, she and Gabriela watch as Agent Robinson interrogates Agent Collins in regards to the president's death. When she fails to make any headway, Sinatra sends in Gabriela, who manages to get Xavier to admit that he's happy the president is dead, however, she doesn't believe that he killed the president, which is good enough for Sinatra who simply puts Agent Collins on a two week leave with plans to reassign him.[1] Sinatra and Agent Robinson stand in on Cal's autopsy. The coroner determines he died from blunt force trauma, and that the murder weapon was some sort of heavy, jagged object, possibly a rock given the soil samples they recovered. Seeing him in this state causes both Sinatra and Robinson to vomit in the bathroom. They also swabbed his nails for DNA, but they won't get the results back for another day or two. In the meantime, Sinatra instructs Robinson to find the killer before Cal is buried and to recover his tablet, though she's concerned about Robinson's state of mind given that she and Cal were having an affair.[3] Killing Billy[] Sinatra warns Billy Sinatra receives an unexpected visit from Agent Pace. He confront her for sending him out onto the surface to kill Susan Donnelly and the others explorers sent to the surface to make contact in order to keep everyone scared so they give up hope of ever leaving. Even if the conditions are technically livable on the surface, they're not hospitable, they're closer to a Third World planet. The best place to be if you want anything remotely resembling a decent life on earth, is there in Paradise. While Billy may have pulled the trigger, he calls Sinatra the monster. She argues otherwise. He tells Sinatra that she's going to leave Xavier alone or else they will have a problem. She reminds Billy that he's nothing more than a killer, and that it's the only reason he was spared. She informs Billy that he is not the only killer she brought down there. If she's going to send someone to kill him, he instructs her that she "better make sure it's the biggest motherf*cker you got." And she does just that by sending Jane to kill him and making it look like an overdose.[4] Waring with Xavier[] Sinatra looks to the artificial sky to see it lit up in red text that says, "They're lying to you."[5] The following day, she learns from the control tower that someone has locked them out of the system. Sinatra calls Gabriela into her office, under the impression that she was at least aware of Xavier's plan, but she quickly discovers that Gabriela is clueless. However, somehow she's aware that Xavier and Gabriela had sex in the shower, meaning that she must have cameras in Gabriela's home. Upon learning that Xavier cut off his tracking band, as well as his kids', she discovers that Robinson is in cahoots with him and used her band to access the south east basement door, where Sinatra keeps the secret cache of weapons. Sinatra tells Xavier his wife is alive Sinatra is forced to make a decision, she can either let this play out or shut down the sky and turn it back on, a hard system reboot but they have no way of knowing how long it will be off and it will send them into complete darkness, which Gabriela warns Sinatra against doing. She initially holds off on the reboot but the text in the sky changes to "Who is Sinatra?" as They Can't Take That Away From Me by Frank Sinatra begins playing over the loudspeaker. Sinatra, terrified of what comes next, as Xavier shoots flares at the tower, instructs Morton to shut down the system, a complete reboot, sending them into darkness despite Gabriela's efforts. with the reboot initiated, so is the shelter protocol. And so Sinatra, Gabriela and all the billionaires are to be escorted to safety but Gabriela realizes this is part of Xavier's plan and so Sinatra reroutes to her house and waits for Xavier. Once he arrives, she admits that while she did kill Billy, she insists that she did not kill the president. Sinatra then grabs a recorder and reveals that Xavier's wife Teri is alive. And if he stops what he's doing, Sinatra will help find her.[6] While being held at gunpoint, Sinatra admits that she did have the four explorers killed because they were bringing a survivor back to the bunker. But before their death, the expedition set up shortwave transmission so they could communicate while they were outside. The transmitters are still active, and Sinatra has been listening to them, playing several recordings from various survivors looking for refuge and creating their own communities, including Teri. Furthering her leverage, Sinatra also has Presley. Sinatra then reveals that the DNA from Cal's murder didn't match anyone from the bunker. It appears the killer came from the outside, but Xavier is concerned about his daughter. Sinatra demands that Xavier release her people, return her arsenal of weapons, and find out who murdered the president. And he will do all this if he wishes to see his daughter or wife again.[2] Xavier threatens to shoot Sinatra With the system rebooted and back under their control, Sinatra calls Jane while wrestling with what they are going to do with Presley. She already knows too much. She can point to Jane, which will point to Sinatra. Jane is eager to handle the matter, but Sinatra simply wants to keep a lid on everything for the time being. With the president being dead and Jane doing everything asked of her, she's hoping Sinatra will allow her to have the president's video game collection, particularly the Wii but Sinatra doesn't even entertain Jane any further and tells her to simply not do anything to Presley for the time being, though Jane hangs up abruptly, leading Sinatra to believe that Jane killed the girl after getting a message from Jane telling her that she handled it and that the problem has been eliminated. When Xavier returns with the identity of Cal's killer, Trent, the librarian who is now dead, he then asks for his daughter but Sinatra is hesitant to answer. She apologizes and says she never intended for things to go this far. Xavier grabs a gun from his ankle holster and kills both of her guards before turning the gun on Sinatra. He asks what she did, but before she can answer, Jane shoots her, leaving Sinatra gasping for air and unable to speak. She reveals that Presley is safe and with Agent Brooks and Rainey. Once Xavier leaves, Jane leans in close to Sinatra and says that she should have just let her have the Wii.[7] Personality[] Sinatra is a woman of influence, as fascinating as she is formidable. A self-made billionaire and a central figure in the underground bunker, she embodies authority grounded in strategic intelligence, pragmatism, and unwavering will. Sinatra is a natural leader: charismatic on the surface, calculating in the shadows. She knows how to inspire loyalty while cultivating fear, treating every situation as a move on a chessboard. Convinced that survival demands difficult choices, she embraces a flexible morality, where manipulation, deceit, and sacrifice become necessary tools for maintaining order. Behind her mask of cold assurance, however, lies a deep emotional fragility, shaped by loss and the heavy burden of responsibility, silently influencing her decisions.
